## Hi, I'm Emily

I was first introduced to data science in Intro to Data Science with R at
Willamette University, and I have been chasing the same feeling ever since: the
moment a messy pile of exports turns into a chart that settles an argument.

Two summers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory are where that got serious. I
validated aerosol datasets, built a pyrocumulonimbus match database, and worked
with GOES satellite imagery to trace how black and brown carbon evolve inside
smoke plumes. That is also where I fell for geospatial data, and it has followed
me into everything since.

Reading is the other thread. In high school the public library was where I could
always get books, and that access is what drew me to my
[capstone](capstone.qmd): making sure the right resources stay within reach of
the people who rely on them. Seven publisher usage reports, five platforms, two
versions of the same reporting standard, and a stakeholder who needs a
defensible answer.

Lately my focus has been data engineering, the unglamorous work of getting
inconsistent sources into one honest table before anyone draws a conclusion from
it. I would rather spend a week making a pipeline reproducible than an afternoon
making a chart that nobody can rebuild.

### Beyond the terminal

- I am into D&D, video games, and more movies and shows than I will admit to.
- I am currently learning data engineering: Airflow, dbt, and warehouse design.
- In a perfect world, I would love to go back to NASA JPL working with geospatial data.
